To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the binary splitting method can be used to compute high-precision mathematical constant values; (2) OmniRPC can be used to implement the independent binary splitting method on a cluster and a grid environment; and (3) the computation of the mathematical constant π can be accelerated by using a cluster and grid environment.
we successfully computed the digits of the mathematical constant π to a precision of 2.5 billion decimal digits and the mathematical constant e to a precision of more than one billion decimal digits.
we successfully achieved nearly linear scalability of our program using a grid RPC mechanism.

the computation of mathematical constants using a combination of a supercomputer and a grid environment.
the computation of high- precision mathematical constants in a grid computing environment.
how to effectively utilize the grid computing environment for the computation of mathematical constants.

the use of grid computing in combination with a binary splitting method is effective for the high-precision computation of mathematical constants.
the grid RPC-based binary splitting method has a significant potential for the computation of high- precision mathematical constants in the future.
this paper has demonstrated that the use of the binary splitting method in combination with grid computing can significantly reduce computation time for large numbers of digits.

our system can reduce the computation time by more than 90% compared to the case where only the supercomputer is used.

the grid RPC system is useful for implementing a parallel computation algorithm in a grid environment.
